read.says: Vera closed at $29.50 on Wednesday and traded at $34.43 by 7:59 p.m. ET (+16.72%); Vertex fell 6.95% after hours to $524.94 from $564.12. Trutakna won accelerated approval on July 7, 2026 and brought in $10.3 million in its first partial quarter, about half of it pharmacies building stock; Vera lost $93.7 million in the third quarter and had $384.0 million of cash and securities at September 30, about $459 million after a $75 million debt draw. Vertex's drug is dosed once every four weeks against Trutakna's weekly injection. Vertex did not say what the FDA asked for; its own warning says approval may not come by the new date or at all. Vera's Wednesday close was 41.75% below its close of December 31, 2025.

themes.beneath: The numbers put the jump in proportion. Trutakna sold $10.3 million in its first partial quarter and about half of that was pharmacies building stock (s4); three more months alone is worth one more quarter of sales of that order. Vera gained about $0.35 bn of market value (16.7% of $2.1 bn; n:VERA). My inference: the price is paying for more than three months of sales, namely a higher chance that Vertex's approval slips further or comes with a narrower label. Vertex gave no reason for the FDA's request, and its own warning says approval may not come by the new date or at all (s4). A correction to last night's note: Vera is not short of money. It lost $93.7 million in the third quarter and held $384.0 million of cash and securities at September 30, about $459 million after a $75 million loan: four to five quarters of such losses, not the half quarter the case file's cash line shows, which leaves out investments (s4, n:VERA). The mosaic's 6.7% chance of a share sale in 20 sessions was read before the jump and stands as printed (z:VERA). Vera's close on Wednesday was still 41.75% below where it ended 2025, which the article reads as fear of this rival (s4, opinion).
themes.cause: Unchanged since last night (t1): the FDA's target date for Vertex's povetacicept moved from Nov 30, 2026 to no later than Feb 28, 2027. Vertex -7.3% and Vera +16.7% in Wednesday's late session, and neither has traded since (s2, s3). A fuller account came this morning (s4).
themes.mechanism: The delay gives Vera's Trutakna up to three more months alone on the market. This morning's account adds what the delay does not change: Vertex's drug is given once every four weeks and Vera's once a week, so the rival that is coming is the more convenient one (s4).
